reasoning_content:
The app is a static web app. The installation guide requires a webserver and Elasticsearch service as prerequisites. The summary notes no Elasticsearch installed — but the guide lists Elasticsearch as a prerequisite. However, is ES part of "installing Index Data Explorer"? The app is purely static; the guide says prerequisites include Elasticsearch Service. The question is whether the absence of ES makes the installation incomplete.

The guide's steps are just copying folders. The prerequisite is Elasticsearch Service — but that's an external service, not part of the project. The task defines success as "the software is installed correctly, completely and operational according to the supplied guide." The app itself is a static frontend. Without ES it cannot query data, but ES is an external service prerequisite, not software being installed. The summary explicitly notes ES not installed as a limitation.

Let me verify the app actually renders. Without a browser, I can't run JS. But I can check module loading. Let me at least verify no syntax errors in module graph and that M.Collapsible etc. Actually let me check if there's a headless browser available to properly verify operational.

No node, no chromium. Can I install? No — prohibited. So I can only do static verification.

Let me check whether the app makes an ES call on load. ProfilingController init queries ES for indices. Let me check.

Actually the operational aspect: page loads and initializes. Without ES, the index dropdown will be empty and errors shown, but the page itself operational. The guide explicitly lists ES as prerequisite; not part of install. The installation method (serve static files) is complete.

I think the appropriate verdict is success with the caveat that ES is an external prerequisite. But let me consider: is the missing top-level `data` folder an issue? Guide says "Additionally you need a folder _data_ on toplevel for specific instances, e.g. for some pages in examples/kosis". The summary says data folders exist inside examples/*/data. Let me check whether kosis pages reference a top-level data path.

Let me investigate.
